1	"""
2	A collection of update operations for TinyDB.
3	
4	They are used for updates like this:
5	
6	>>> db.update(delete('foo'), where('foo') == 2)
7	
8	This would delete the ``foo`` field from all documents where ``foo`` equals 2.
9	"""
10	
11	
12	from collections.abc import Callable, MutableMapping
13	from typing import Any, Union
14	
15	
16	def delete(field: str) -> Callable[[MutableMapping], None]:
17	    """
18	    Delete a given field from the document.
19	    """
20	    def transform(doc: MutableMapping):
21	        del doc[field]
22	
23	    return transform
24	
25	
26	def add(field: str, n: Union[int, float, str]) -> Callable[[MutableMapping], None]:
27	    """
28	    Add ``n`` to a given field in the document.
29	
30	    Also works for strings (concatenation), matching the documented behavior.
31	    """
32	    def transform(doc: MutableMapping):
33	        doc[field] += n
34	
35	    return transform
36	
37	
38	def subtract(field: str, n: Union[int, float]) -> Callable[[MutableMapping], None]:
39	    """
40	    Subtract ``n`` to a given field in the document.
41	    """
42	    def transform(doc: MutableMapping):
43	        doc[field] -= n
44	
45	    return transform
46	
47	
48	def set(field: str, val: Any) -> Callable[[MutableMapping], None]:
49	    """
50	    Set a given field to ``val``.
51	    """
52	    def transform(doc: MutableMapping):
53	        doc[field] = val
54	
55	    return transform
56	
57	
58	def increment(field: str) -> Callable[[MutableMapping], None]:
59	    """
60	    Increment a given field in the document by 1.
61	    """
62	    def transform(doc: MutableMapping):
63	        doc[field] += 1
64	
65	    return transform
66	
67	
68	def decrement(field: str) -> Callable[[MutableMapping], None]:
69	    """
70	    Decrement a given field in the document by 1.
71	    """
72	    def transform(doc: MutableMapping):
73	        doc[field] -= 1
74	
75	    return transform
76

input.summary: Add a single `append(field, value)` factory to tinydb/operations.py that returns a `transform(doc)` closure which appends to the list in `field` and creates `[value]` when the field is missing.
input.approach: Follow the existing operations convention (factory returning a `transform(doc)` closure that mutates the doc in place and returns None). Implement as `doc.setdefault(field, []).append(value)`. A missing field becomes `[value]` (FR-OPS-002), an existing list gets the value added at the end (FR-OPS-001), and a list-valued `value` is added as one element (ASM-001 / FR-OPS-003). A non-list existing value raises the natural AttributeError (ASM-002 / Q-001 default (a)). Do not call the module's `set` or any builtin shadowed by it. Update the module docstring only if desired; no docs/changelog changes, since Q-003 is unanswered and docs are out of scope. Table.update already runs the transform on each matching document and persists through `_update_table`, so no changes to table.py are needed.

alternatives.option: Explicit `if field not in doc: doc[field] = [value] else: doc[field].append(value)`
alternatives.why_not: More lines for the same behaviour; setdefault is shorter and equally clear.

alternatives.option: Raise TypeError when the existing value is not a list, or replace it, or treat None as missing (Q-001 b/c/d)
alternatives.why_not: Not requested; spec default is (a), natural Python error, consistent with the other operations. Adds behaviour that has no acceptance criterion.

alternatives.option: Extend semantics for list/tuple values (Q-002 b)
alternatives.why_not: Spec default and FR-OPS-003 use list.append semantics; the name `append` implies it.
Fails with non-list types differently and needlessly copies the list; in-place append matches the issue's own snippet.

alternatives.option: Also update docs/usage.rst, docs/api.rst and docs/changelog.rst
alternatives.why_not: Q-003 is unanswered (maintainer decision) and the spec lists docs as out of scope.

files.purpose: Add the new `append` update operation next to the existing operations.

symbols.name: append
symbols.description: `append(field: str, value: Any) -> Callable[[MutableMapping], None]`. Returns an inner `transform(doc)` that does `doc.setdefault(field, []).append(value)`. It creates the field as `[value]` when missing, appends to the end of an existing list, and does not flatten list values. It has a docstring in the style of the other operations.

ac_mapping.test_idea: TinyDB(storage=MemoryStorage) with ids 7 and 8; update(append('tags','urgent'), Query().id == 7); assert doc 7 tags == ['a','urgent'] and doc 8 tags == ['b'].
`from tinydb.operations import append` succeeds and `callable(append)` is True.
Doc {'id':7,'tags':[]}; update with append('tags','urgent'); assert tags == ['urgent'].
Two docs with tags ['a'] and ['b']; update(append('tags','x'), Query().id.exists()); assert tags == ['a','x'] and ['b','x'].
Doc {'id':7} with no tags; update with append; assert tags == ['urgent'] and no exception.
Docs {'id':7} and {'id':8}; update only id 7; assert doc 7 tags == ['urgent'] and 'tags' not in doc 8.
Docs {'id':7} and {'id':8,'tags':['a']}; update with Query().id.exists(); assert ['urgent'] and ['a','urgent'].
Doc tags ['a']; append('tags', ['x','y']); assert tags == ['a', ['x','y']] (assumption-only AC, list.append semantics).

constraints.how_respected: No storage changes; the operation is storage-agnostic.
Not a query operation, so no query hash is needed. Queries are untouched.
The operation only mutates the document passed in by Table.update; persistence and cache invalidation still happen in `Table._update_table`. Nothing writes to storage directly.
operations.py gains no new imports (Any and MutableMapping are already imported) and nothing imports table/database.
Standard library only; no new dependencies.

risks: Non-list existing values (string, number, None) raise AttributeError (Q-001, default (a)); a maintainer may later want TypeError or replacement.
A list/tuple argument is appended as a single nested element (ASM-001); the maintainer might prefer extend semantics.
Module-level `set` in operations.py shadows the builtin, so the implementation must not use `set()` and should use setdefault, as designed.

The append mutates the list object in place. With MemoryStorage, if a user inserted a list they still hold a reference to, that list may be mutated, because MemoryStorage does not copy. This is the same aliasing as the existing operations and is acceptable.
Docs and changelog are not updated (Q-003 unanswered), so the new operation is undocumented until a maintainer decides.
